ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Tā Moko: A Record of an Individual's Path

fullPassage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.

questions.passage: Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are ①<u>added</u> to their tattoos to ②<u>reflect</u> their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great ③<u>importance</u> as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to ④<u>discard</u> their traditions and heritage for the next generation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마오리족은 전통과 유산을 보존하기를(preserve) 희망한다. discard(버리다)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ①added: 원문 그대로
✅ ②reflect: 원문 그대로
✅ ③importance: 원문 그대로
❌ ④discard: 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: preserve(보존하다) ↔ discard(버리다). rite of passage = 통과 의례. heritage = 유산.

questions.passage: Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most (A)[sacred / ordinary] part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their (B)[entire / partial] faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are (C)[added / removed] to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 머리를 가장 신성한 부분으로 여겼다. 남자는 얼굴 전체에 문신한다. 나이가 들수록 더 많은 선과 모양이 추가된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② sacred — entire — added
❌ ① ordinary — entire — removed
❌ ③ sacred — partial — removed
❌ ④ ordinary — partial — added
✅ (A) sacred: 원문 그대로 '신성한'. 머리를 신성시해 얼굴에 문신하는 맥락. ordinary(평범한)는 반대. ✅ (B) entire: 원문 그대로 '전체'. 남성은 얼굴 전체, 여성은 입술과 턱만이라는 대비. partial(부분적)은 반대. ✅ (C) added: 원문 그대로 '추가된다'. 경험이 쌓이면 문신이 추가되는 것이지 removed(제거)되는 것이 아님.
det.tip: sacred(신성한) ↔ ordinary(평범한). entire(전체의) ↔ partial(부분적인). add(추가하다) ↔ remove(제거하다).

questions.passage: It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko (A)[represents / conceals] a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less (B)[common / rare] these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to (C)[preserve / abandon] their traditions and heritage for the next generation. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 각 곡선은 족보, 사회적 지위, 업적을 나타낸다. 요즘은 덜 흔하지만 전통을 보존하기 위해 행해진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ represents — common — preserve
❌ ② conceals — common — abandon
❌ ① represents — rare — abandon
❌ ④ conceals — rare — preserve
✅ (A) represents: 원문 그대로 '나타내다'. conceals(숨기다)는 문신의 표현적 기능과 반대. ✅ (B) common: 원문 'less common(덜 흔한)'. less rare(덜 드문)는 '더 흔한'이 되어 반대. ✅ (C) preserve: 원문 그대로 '보존하다'. abandon(포기하다)은 전통 계승 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: represent(나타내다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). common(흔한) ↔ rare(드문). preserve(보존하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다).

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally ①<u>significant</u> practice of the Maori for thousands of years. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa, social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the ③<u>same</u>. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most ④<u>trivial</u> part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 마오리족은 머리를 신체에서 가장 신성한(sacred) 부분으로 여겼다. trivial(사소한)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①significant(중요한): 수천 년간 지속된 문화적 관행으로 적절. ✅ ②symbolic(상징적인): 개인의 여정을 상징한다는 맥락 적절. ✅ ③same(같은): 두 타 모코가 같지 않다는 원문 그대로. ❌ ④trivial(사소한): 원문은 sacred(신성한). 신성하기 때문에 얼굴에 문신하는 것이므로 trivial은 반대.
det.tip: sacred(신성한) ↔ trivial(사소한). the most sacred part = 가장 신성한 부분.

det.analysis:

❌ ② trivial — decorative — failures

❌ ④ trivial — destructive — accomplishments

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이것이 왜 두 타 모코 디자인이 똑같아 보이지 않는지를 설명해 준다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①same: 원문 'no two tā moko designs look the same'. 개인의 고유한 족보/업적을 반영하므로 같은 디자인이 없다. ❌ ②different: 'no two ~ look the different'는 문법적으로 불가. ❌ ③beautiful: 외모 묘사가 아닌 고유성에 대한 설명. ❌ ④traditional: 전통적으로 보인다는 뜻이 되어 문맥 불일치.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 common과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 타 모코는 요즘 덜 흔하지만 여전히 행해진다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②rare(드문): common(흔한)의 반의어. ❌ ①frequent(빈번한): 동의어. ❌ ③popular(인기 있는): 유사 의미. ❌ ④ordinary(평범한): 유사 의미로 '흔한'과 비슷.
det.tip: common = frequent = ordinary (흔한) ↔ rare = scarce = uncommon (드문).

questions.passage:
(A) Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of <u>passage</u> throughout their lives.

(B) There is a narrow <u>passage</u> leading from the entrance to the main hall.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 passage와 (B)의 passage가 각각 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 'rite of passage'에서 passage = 과정, 전환(통과 의례). (B) 'a narrow passage leading from the entrance'에서 passage = 통로, 복도.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: (A) rite of passage는 '통과 의례'로 passage=과정/전환. (B) a narrow passage는 '좁은 통로'로 passage=통로. ❌ ①: (A)와 (B) 의미가 뒤바뀜. ❌ ②④: 문단(paragraph)의 의미는 이 맥락과 무관.
det.tip: passage: ① 통로(= corridor) ② 과정/전환(rite of passage) ③ 문단(a passage from the book). 다의어.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"regarded as holy and deserving of respect, especially in connection with religion or a deity"

det.korean: 종교나 신과 관련하여 신성하고 존경받을 가치가 있는 것으로 여겨지는 = sacred(신성한).
det.analysis: ✅ ④sacred(신성한): 영영 정의와 정확히 일치. ❌ ①symbolic(상징적인): 상징적이지 신성함과 다름. ❌ ②decorative(장식적인): 장식과 신성은 다른 개념. ❌ ③cultural(문화적인): 문화와 신성은 다른 개념.
det.tip: sacred: 신성한 (= holy, divine). 마오리족에게 머리는 가장 sacred한 신체 부위.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice. It is not only decorative but also __________ (symbol) of an individual's journey from their past to their present.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 장식적일 뿐만 아니라 개인의 여정을 상징하는(symbolic) 것이기도 하다.
det.analysis: symbol(명사: 상징) → symbolic(형용사: 상징적인). 'not only decorative(형용사) but also __(형용사)' 병렬 구조에서 형용사 필요.
det.tip: symbol(명사) → symbolic(형용사) → symbolize(동사). not only A but also B: A와 B는 같은 품사.

questions.passage: The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos. Tattooing __________ (traditional) held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 문신은 전통적으로(traditionally) 삶의 통과 의례로서 큰 중요성을 지녔다.
det.analysis: traditional(형용사: 전통적인) → traditionally(부사: 전통적으로). 동사 held를 수식하는 부사가 필요.
det.tip: tradition(명사) → traditional(형용사) → traditionally(부사). 부사는 동사를 수식.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly ____. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 머리를 가장 신성한 부분으로 여겨 주로 얼굴에 문신한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①tattoo their faces: 머리가 신성 → 얼굴에 문신. 다음 문장의 남녀별 얼굴 문신 위치와도 연결. ❌ ②tattoo their arms: 머리가 신성한데 팔에 문신하는 것은 비논리적. ❌ ③paint their bodies: 문신(tattooing)이지 페인팅이 아님. ❌ ④cover their heads: 문신과 덮는 것은 다른 행위.
det.tip: so(그래서)는 인과관계. 원인: 머리=신성 → 결과: 얼굴에 문신.

questions.passage: Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing, which has been a culturally significant practice of the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only decorative but also symbolic of an individual's journey from their past to their present. Each curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a person's whakapapa (genealogy), social positions, and personal accomplishments. This explains why no two tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the Maori have considered the head to be the most sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire faces, while women have it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā moko is less common these days, it is still practiced today by Maori people, who hope to ____.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation
attract more tourists to their country
replace traditional designs with new ones

det.korean: 마오리족은 다음 세대를 위해 전통과 유산을 보존하기를 희망한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②preserve their traditions and heritage for the next generation: 원문 그대로. 비록 덜 흔해졌지만 전통 보존을 위해 여전히 행한다는 맥락. ❌ ①modernize: 현대화가 아닌 보존이 핵심. ❌ ③attract tourists: 관광이 아닌 문화 계승의 맥락. ❌ ④replace: 교체가 아닌 유지/보존.
det.tip: preserve: 보존하다. heritage: 유산. Although ~, still ~: 양보/역접 구문.
